speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness, could you please describe exactly where the pain radiates and whether you have noticed any numbness or tingling in specific fingers?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient's history of diabetes and the specific location of symptoms (neck, arms, hands) with progressive weakness strongly suggest a compressive myelopathy. Given his age and chronic conditions, could you tell me if you are experiencing any difficulty with bowel or bladder control, or have you noticed weakness in your legs as well?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Anterior Horn Cell involvement (Cervical Spondylomyelopathy).

The combination of long-standing neck/arm pain, paresthesias, bilateral hand weakness, fasciculations, and absent reflexes in a patient with diabetes suggests a mixed picture of cervical cord compression (myelopathy) and possible anterior horn cell damage. I request immediate MRI of the Cervical Spine to visualize the cord compression and signal changes.
